ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Johnny Cash

code.originalText: Endocrinology consultation for diabetes and autonomic neuropathy

text.paragraph: Endocrinology consultation and four-week diabetes check: lightheadedness on standing and choice of add-on glucose-lowering therapy. [S]

Mr. Cash is a 71-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, autonomic and peripheral neuropathy, and severe primary open-angle glaucoma, seen four weeks after his first visit for an endocrinology consultation on the same day as his diabetes check. Metformin was raised to 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin was started, and dorzolamide was added to latanoprost four weeks ago. He takes all of them, and metformin causes no stomach upset. His fasting home glucose readings run 140 to 170 mg/dL, with none below 70. He now stands up in stages, has raised the head of his bed, wears waist-high compression, and drinks about 2 liters a day. He is still lightheaded on standing most mornings and after meals, but he has had no further falls since the first visit. He asks again what he really has, since he was once told it was Shy-Drager syndrome. [S]

list.item:
Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension from diabetic autonomic neuropathy (I95.1). A fall of 32 mmHg in systolic pressure on standing with a rise of only 4 beats per minute in heart rate shows a neurogenic cause. With long-standing diabetes and length-dependent sensory loss in both legs, the pattern fits diabetic autonomic neuropathy, and the earlier Shy-Drager label is not carried forward in this record. He is still symptomatic despite non-drug measures, and lying pressure is 150/84 mmHg. [S]
Start midodrine 2.5 mg on waking, at midday, and mid-afternoon, with the last dose at least four hours before bed.
Continue staged standing, head-of-bed elevation, compression, and fluids.
Check lying, seated, and standing pressure at each visit.

Type 2 diabetes with diabetic autonomic neuropathy (E11.43). HbA1c 8.6% four weeks ago, above his goal below 7.5%; fasting readings 140 to 170 on full-dose metformin. Sulfonylureas and insulin are avoided because autonomic neuropathy may blunt the warning signs of low glucose. eGFR 72 allows full-dose sitagliptin. Seated pressure is above 130/80, but with orthostatic hypotension no blood pressure medicine is used. [S]
Start sitagliptin 100 mg daily.
Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
HbA1c at the three-month review.

Diabetic peripheral neuropathy with loss of protective sensation (E11.42). No ulcer or pre-ulcerative lesion. [S]
Daily foot checks and protective shoes.

Primary open-angle glaucoma, severe stage (H40.1133). Dorzolamide added four weeks ago; no eye pressure check has been made since. [S]
Ask the eye clinic for a pressure check as soon as possible.
